title: Obama Seeking $19 Billion for National Cybersecurity

image.attribution: DoD photo by U.S. Air Force Staff Sgt. Marianique Santos / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
U.S. President Barack Obama announced a national cybersecurity plan, calling cyber threats among “the most urgent dangers to America’s economic and national security.”

The “Cybersecurity National Action Plan” is the administration’s attempt to build a broad, cohesive federal response to cyberthreats. It calls for an increase in spending on cybersecurity across all U.S. government agencies to $19 billion, an increase of 35 percent over last year.

The plan calls for the creation of a new high-level federal position to coordinate cybersecurity across civilian agencies and working with military and intelligence counterparts in tracking down cyber intruders in federal networks. Private-sector businesses have long had positions similar to the one proposed by the administration.

“The nation’s cyber adversaries are getting more sophisticated every day. ... We have to be even more nimble and resilient, and stay ahead of these threats,” Obama wrote.

The goal of the cybersecurity plan is to provide “every American a basic level of online security,” he added.

The budget proposal also calls for $62 million to expand efforts to attract and retain qualified cyber professionals working for the government.

Cybersecurity has become a top public issue following several high-profile hacks of private companies, such as the Target retail chain stores, and federal agencies, such as the breach last year of the personal information of 21 million current and retired federal employees held by the Office of Personnel Management.

questions.question: What does the “Cybersecurity National Action Plan” represent?
options: A comprehensive strategy to enhance public awareness about internet safety.
An initiative aimed at improving the coordination of cybersecurity efforts between federal and private sectors.
A budget proposal for federal agencies to limit their cybersecurity spending.
A plan that focuses solely on military cybersecurity operations.
questions.answer: An initiative aimed at improving the coordination of cybersecurity efforts between federal and private sectors.

questions.question: How much money does Obama want to be invested in cybersecurity?
options: $19 billion, which reflects an increase compared to last year.
$15 billion, emphasizing a decrease in previous spending.
$62 million for specific projects focused only on military cybersecurity.
$35 billion to cover both cybersecurity and technology initiatives.
questions.answer: $19 billion, which reflects an increase compared to last year.

questions.question: Why does Obama want to implement this system?
options: To prevent potential lawsuits against the government from cybersecurity breaches.
To ensure that every American has access to a standardized level of online security.
To allocate funds to military-based cybersecurity initiatives only.
To limit cybersecurity measures to federal employees and agencies.
questions.answer: To ensure that every American has access to a standardized level of online security.
